newsitem.title: ISRAEL: "I'm their Dad," Israel PM says of kids' US trip.
newsitem.headline: "I'm their Dad," Israel PM says of kids' US trip.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday defended taking his two young sons on an official U.S. trip, brushing aside criticism he was making a public spectacle of them.

The thrice-married leader, who has admitted cheating on his present wife Sara, is accused by media and public alike of drawing unprecedented attention to his home life in a bid to portray himself as a family man.

"I am practically convinced you won't like this question but you surely are aware that a lot of people are asking it: Why did you take your children to America?" Israel's Channel Two asked Netanyahu on his air-force plane to Washington.

"I'm their Dad, and my wife and I want to be with our children. And I am telling you I will take them whenever I can," said Netanyahu, who later carried one of the two boys, aged 5 and 2, off the plane in Washington.
"I don't intend to meet my children in another few years and have them ask me who is that man appearing on television," Netanyahu said in the interview broadcast on Thursday.
